title: Advanced UNSW Hierarchical Performance Engineering Plan (design only)
commands_run: All other evidence reused from the A9.65 read-only audit (no new training/eval/preprocess executed)

a9_6_recap.verdict: Failed as a Head 2 improvement; binary up, Head 2 + rare down; do not replace A9.

already_strong: Binary Head 1 is strong and near-saturated: macro-F1 0.894, F1 0.910, attack recall 0.949, only 5.1% of attacks missed.
Pipeline is clean and leakage-free: train-only class weights, validation-only checkpoint selection, single final test, correct attack-row masking, ignore_index=-1.
Metrics are honest: macro-F1 over the full fixed 9-class set (never-predicted classes score 0), Head 2 scored on attack rows only, routed end-to-end view also reported. No inflation.
Strong families already: Generic 0.981, Reconnaissance 0.823, Fuzzers 0.768, Exploits 0.691.
Well-instrumented and reproducible: per-epoch history, confusion matrices, routing summary, manifest, class-weight snapshot, model summary.
weak_points: Head 2 attack-family macro-F1 0.500, held down by Analysis (F1 0.012) and Backdoor (F1 0.070), and DoS (0.388).
Rare-class precision is low: Shellcode 0.308, Worms 0.221 (high recall, low precision from class weighting).
Wrong-family attribution is the dominant blocker: 22.8% of attacks are detected-but-wrong-family vs only 5.1% missed-as-benign.
Head 2 holds only ~0.23% of model parameters (single Linear(128,9)) on an embedding shaped mostly by the easy binary task.
do_not_change: Binary Head 1 and binary BCE loss (strong; do not risk it).
Corrected UNSW protocol, input_dim 192, attack_head_dim 9, masking, ignore_index=-1.
Train-only class weights, validation-only selection, single final test, metric definitions.
Oversampling stays disabled (project policy + precision risk).

model_architecture.evidence: Encoder ~512k params; Head 2 = single Linear(128,9) ~1,161 params (0.23%). Binary loss saturates early (train 0.077, val macro ~0.93 flat) while Head 2 val macro-F1 plateaus ~0.59.

head2_capacity.evidence: Confusion matrix shows wrong-family attribution into DoS/Backdoor sinks; one linear layer cannot model non-linear family boundaries in a binary-dominated embedding.

loss_design.evidence: Global attack_loss_weight is blunt; A9.6 (1.5) lowered rare precision (Shellcode 0.308->0.236) and did not separate Analysis/Backdoor -> macro down. Loss masking/weight wiring itself is correct.
loss_design.expected_impact: explains A9.6; warns focal+weights risks the same

class_weight_strategy.evidence: sqrt-inverse-frequency mean-normalized cap=10 (max used 3.95 for Worms). Rare recall high, precision low -> cap/temperature may over-assign rare classes.

sampler_batch_strategy.evidence: ~0.75 Worms / 6.6 Shellcode per 1024-batch, but rare recall already high; problem is precision, not recall. Balanced sampling/oversampling would not help macro-F1 and could hurt precision.

validation_objective.evidence: val_binary span ~0.013 vs val_attack span ~0.12; the 0.5/0.5 blend lets a near-flat binary term occupy half the selection signal.

optimizer_lr_earlystop.evidence: AdamW lr 1e-3 constant (no scheduler), no grad clip; best epoch 35, ran to max 40; val attack plateaued by ~epoch 19-25.

dropout_regularization.evidence: dropout 0.20, weight_decay 1e-4. Head 2 appears to UNDERFIT (high train attack loss, plateaued val), not overfit, so a stronger Head 2 branch with its own dropout is the right direction.

metric_evaluation.evidence: macro-F1 over full 9 classes; attack-row-only Head 2; teacher-forced headline + harsher routed view; binary macro reconstructs from CM. Professor-facing quality. No metric hides failures.

feature_preprocessing.evidence: 133/192 features are ultra-rare proto one-hots (StandardScaler-scaled). Dilutes signal but easy classes already strong, so not dominant. Changing features alters feature_dim and breaks comparability.

training_history_confusion.evidence: Analysis->DoS 479/677, Backdoor->DoS 409/583, DoS->Exploits 1039; DoS/Backdoor are over-predicted sinks. val->test gap: binary 0.933->0.894, attack 0.592->0.500 (official-partition prior shift, benign 31.9% train vs 44.9% test).
training_history_confusion.expected_impact: explains the ceiling and the gap (largely intrinsic)

single_seed_methodology.evidence: Per-epoch val attack macro-F1 swings +/-0.02-0.03; A9 vs A9.6 differ only 0.015 (N=1). Sub-noise differences are not interpretable.

ranked_options.name: A9.9 attack_weight_cap_down
ranked_options.factor: Lower attack class-weight cap/temperature to reduce rare over-assignment

ranked_options.name: head2_focal_loss
ranked_options.factor: Focal loss (gamma 1.5-2.0) on attack rows, attack_loss_weight back to 1.0

ranked_options.name: feature_cleanup
ranked_options.factor: Prune ultra-rare proto dummies / frequency-encode proto / leave one-hots unscaled
ranked_options.scientific_validity_risk: medium (changes feature_dim; needs separate safety gates)

ranked_options.name: two_stage_head2_finetune
ranked_options.factor: Joint warmup -> freeze/partially fine-tune encoder -> train stronger Head 2 on attack rows

ranked_options.name: threshold_calibration
ranked_options.factor: Calibrate binary decision threshold on validation

ranked_options.name: oversampling_or_balanced_sampler
ranked_options.factor: Duplicate/synthesize or balance-sample minority attack rows

selected_experiment_hypothesis: Giving Head 2 its own small non-linear branch over the shared embedding (without adding minority loss pressure) lets it model the non-linear family boundaries that a single linear layer cannot, improving attack-family macro-F1 over A9 while keeping the strong binary head and rare-class precision stable.
exact_planned_changes: Add a non-linear Head 2 branch: shared_embedding(128) -> Linear(128,128) -> LayerNorm -> GELU -> Dropout(p=model.dropout, default 0.2) -> Linear(128,9).
Keep binary_head as the existing single Linear(128,1).
Make the branch opt-in via a model config flag (e.g. model.head2_hidden_dims: [128]) so A9 behavior is the default when absent.
Run with >=3 seeds; report mean +/- std for headline and rare-class metrics.
unchanged_controls: Loss: masked multi-task; CrossEntropy on attack rows; binary_loss_weight=1.0; attack_loss_weight=1.0
Train-only A8.5/A8.8 class weights and cap=10.0
Shared encoder (256,128,128), gated block, dropout 0.20, LayerNorm, residual_expansion 2
AdamW lr 1e-3, weight_decay 1e-4, batch 1024, max_epochs 40, early-stop patience 6
Corrected UNSW protocol, input_dim 192, attack_head_dim 9, ignore_index -1
expected_realistic_improvement: Modest, honest lift on the overlapping cluster boundaries (DoS/Exploits/Backdoor); little movement expected on Analysis (intrinsic overlap).
why_above_0_9_unrealistic: Analysis/Backdoor/DoS/Exploits overlap by construction on the corrected official UNSW split; honest 9-class macro-F1 in the literature sits ~0.45-0.60. >0.9 would require near-perfect separation of intrinsically-entangled families and is not achievable from these features.

realistic_target_after_1_to_3_experiment.qualitative: Lift at least one of Analysis/Backdoor/DoS off the floor without collapsing Shellcode/Worms precision.

overfitting_risks: A deeper Head 2 branch could memorize rare-class train rows (Worms 109). Mitigation: keep dropout/LayerNorm in the branch, keep the cap, validation-only selection, 3-seed reporting.
Encoder is left unchanged, so shared-representation overfitting risk is unchanged from A9.
scientific_validity_risks: Single-seed promotion would be invalid (deltas within noise). Mitigation: >=3 seeds, promote only beyond the noise band.
Any test-set-informed selection/tuning would invalidate results. Mitigation: validation-only selection, one final test.
Feature changes would break comparability with A9/A9.6. Mitigation: keep features fixed for A9.7; gate feature work separately.
implementation_complexity: low (additive Head 2 branch behind a config flag; trainer/eval/output writers unchanged)
success_criteria: Attack-family macro-F1 (3-seed mean) >= 0.535 and beats A9 beyond the noise band (>= ~0.02 absolute).
Attack false negatives <= 2,450; benign false positives <= 7,000.
Rare-class macro-F1 >= 0.385669; Shellcode F1 >= 0.4099 (precision >= 0.25); Worms F1 >= 0.2814 (precision >= 0.18).
At least one of Analysis/Backdoor/DoS improves over A9 without rare-class collapse.
Training stable, complete, no NaN; A9/A9.6 artifacts untouched; separate output paths used.
failure_criteria: Attack-family macro-F1 fails to beat A9 beyond noise or stays < 0.535 (3-seed mean).
Any binary safety gate fails (macro-F1 < 0.884, F1 < 0.905, FN > 2,450, FP > 7,000).
Rare-class macro-F1 < 0.385669, or Shellcode/Worms precision collapses below floors.
Analysis, Backdoor, and DoS all remain stagnant while strong classes absorb gains.
Training unstable/incomplete/NaN, or any A9/A9.6 artifact overwritten, or non-separate output paths used.
next_task_prompt_summary: After main-review approval: implement Task A9.7 = add an opt-in non-linear Head 2 branch (128->128->9, GELU+LayerNorm+Dropout) behind a model config flag; create configs/training/unsw_nb15_hierarchical_a9_7_head2_branch.yaml (one factor vs A9); train UNSW only with >=3 seeds; write to separate A9.7 output paths; keep A9 frozen; evaluate test once per seed after validation-only selection; compare 3-seed mean +/- std against A9 gates.
